title: Start with Retiam
summary: Choose how to use Retiam and follow the path from a TypeScript scene to an animation video.

blocks.text: Retiam turns TypeScript scene code into 2D and 3D animation. Its main use case is generating animation videos from your own project with Retiam installed as an npm library. Define the objects, choreograph their changes and render the result at the resolution and frame rate you need. WebGPU draws the scene in a browser, including the headless browser used for video rendering.

The same engine can power interactive explanations, simulations and custom GPU visualizations. Start with one scene and a few entities, then add plotting, charts, graphs, physics, procedural shapes or speech as the subject needs them.
Open your first project in Studio

The generator installs a TypeScript project and opens Studio with a Write animation of “Retiam”. Edit src/scenes/Retiam.ts, resize the editor below the preview, then configure video output in config.js. The complete workflow uses create-retiam 1.0.2 or newer and Retiam 1.0.1 or newer. See [project setup](/installation#create-with-studio) for requirements and options.
To produce an MP4, stop the server with Ctrl+C, enter the project folder, and run the renderer. Chrome with WebGPU and FFmpeg on PATH are required for video output.

blocks.code:
cd my-animation
npx retiam render src/scenes/Retiam.ts

blocks.text: The generated config.js contains every render setting at its default. [Render configuration](/export#render-configuration) explains dimensions, fps, duration, shading and command-line overrides.

blocks.text: [Tutorials](/tutorials) walk through a finished result, with prerequisites, editable examples and exercises. Guides explain concepts; API references give exact contracts; the examples catalog collects complete scenes. Follow the guides in order using Previous and Next for a guided sequence.

Guides teach current workflows and contain editable examples. API pages give the source-derived contracts, declared defaults, overloads and runtime rejection paths. The examples catalog includes every TypeScript demo, including supporting data modules. Engineering notebooks preserve all 83 original documents as explicitly identified design and historical references.

Search for a symbol, option, method, shader or demo filename. Cross-links lead to exact API modules. Source links refer to the repository’s `main` branch; the content was generated from this checkout, so compare against the checkout if the remote branch has changed.

blocks.content: The live examples load Retiam through the configured CDN module URL and run editable scene code in the page. Small documentation labs without imports receive the core exports automatically. When moving a scene into your npm project, use explicit package imports and your own assets. See [installation](/installation) for each usage mode.
